target.role: fresh whole-journey belonging and placement discovery for STRANGE GAIT
target.position: Whole journey: before the opener, between every non-protected pair, or after the tail. Preserve only Transparency → When We Froze and When We Froze → Stardancer; Truth in Noise → Transparency remains available.
target.purpose: Test a current vocal bass-world turn, a current Jakarta experimental-techno cut, one recent broken-techno catalogue track and one overlooked acid-techno debut cut against their strongest lawful placements. Character change is allowed; admission still requires purposeful transition, local-run and long-form effect.

sourceWindows: CURRENT / BANDCAMP DAILY JULY 2026: https://daily.bandcamp.com/best-electronic/the-best-electronic-music-on-bandcamp-july-2026 — the 8110118, GRCA., Alex Mein Smith, Anaïs/Stylo G/Lady Leshurr, HVL and adjacent entries were screened. Strong Like Lion and 8110118's V4-4 supplied the strongest fresh exact current identities outside the GRCA/HVL lanes already used.

CURRENT JAKARTA EXPERIMENTAL TECHNO: https://8110118.bandcamp.com/album/jiwa-krungu — all seven tracks on the 2026-07-23 album were screened. V4-4 retained as the exact closing cut; only album-level genre/form evidence and track-specific field-recording credit are asserted.

RECENT OVERLOOKED CATALOGUE / PURELINK: https://ra.co/reviews/35710 — the Signs album review was screened. Pinned retained because the review gives exact-track evidence of patient broken techno whose beat gradually dismantles.

DEEP CATALOGUE / THE BUNKER NEW YORK: https://daily.bandcamp.com/best-electronic/bandcamp-best-electronic-june-2018 — Abby Echiverri's four-track debut EP was screened. Ionosfeer retained because the review identifies it specifically as jagged within a broader acid-techno language of fragmented rhythm.

ADDITIONAL WINDOWS: Bandcamp Daily's September 4, 2026 Essential Releases, July 2026 monthly list, May and August 2018 electronic lists, and current Bandcamp/Resident Advisor search results were screened. Groove Armada, Alex Mein Smith, Chairman Kato, Facta, HVL, Posthuman and other nearby releases were not promoted because evidence was release-level, outside the volume lens, or weaker than the selected four.
explorationReceipt.approximateInspectedScope: Approximately 44 named tracks across current, adjacent, emerging and overlooked catalogue windows; metadata and attributed descriptions only, with zero audio auditions.
exclusions: All 14 canonical identities, active placement-specific rejects and every untriggered PARKED revisit were excluded. Exact identities and primary discovery lanes retained in Runs 53–64 were not recycled.
The protected internal handoffs Transparency → When We Froze and When We Froze → Stardancer remain unavailable; Truth in Noise → Transparency and every other boundary remain available.

No lead was promoted for recency, artist or label reputation, genre, novelty, title or technical cleverness. BPM, energy, density, space, hypnosis, phrase structure, harmonic relation and mixability remain unknown unless explicitly stated.
Album-level evidence for V4-4 is marked as such and is not converted into track-specific sonic fact. The other three leads have exact-track descriptions from identified reviews.
rankedLeadSummary: 1. Purelink — Pinned: strongest structural case, with exact evidence that a patient broken-techno beat dismantles over time.
2. Abby Echiverri — Ionosfeer: strongest overlooked techno case, with exact evidence of jagged construction inside a fragmented acid-techno debut.
3. Anaïs, Stylo G & Lady Leshurr — Strong Like Lion: strongest current different-world case, with exact evidence of 140-BPM bass-warping, dancehall vocals and club intent.
4. 8110118 — V4-4: strongest current experimental-techno research case, but with deliberately limited exact-track evidence.
